frontier.hypothesis: A zero-instruction-cost C spelling exists that makes reg_n_sets >= 2 for the cam and const pseudos, removing their REG_EQUIV and therefore the x2 doubling, and it lands the byte match from the def-order chassis.
frontier.mechanism: update_equiv_regs (local-alloc.c ~1015-1030) bails out with continue before granting REG_EQUIV whenever reg_n_sets[regno] != 1, and the x2 at local-alloc.c:1064 is gated on that note. reg_n_sets is counted by flow's life_analysis, which runs BEFORE combine/sched/local-alloc, while cross-jumping (jump2) and reload's no-op-move deletion run AFTER — so a second SET that exists at flow time can be absent from the emitted stream.

Success signal readable in that one table: 74 and 76 report livelen in [32,38] with L(74) <= L(76), copy_end 77 at 38, at 72 build insns. Two ranked spellings: (a) two identical assignments placed in cross-jumpable tails — both `if (v0 != 0) goto retry;` sites are candidates, since cross-jump merges identical tails after reload; (b) initialise via a REG-to-REG copy across an EBB boundary so cse attaches no constant REG_EQUAL (cse.c:6923 requires GET_CODE (src_const) != REG), letting optimize_reg_copy_1/2 tie the pseudos and reload delete the move. ALWAYS confirm the insn count is still 72 — rejected/twoset-kills-regequiv-plus2insns.c proves the doubling dies but cost +2.

frontier.hypothesis: The doubled length can instead be pulled back INTO the window by local-alloc's direct live-length arithmetic, leaving the REG_EQUIV in place.
frontier.mechanism: optimize_reg_copy_1, called from the same update_equiv_regs insn loop (local-alloc.c:1003-1015), writes reg_live_length[sregno] -= length and reg_live_length[dregno] += d_length at local-alloc.c:820-831 — the only site besides the x2 that edits a live length after flow. cam at 72 needs to land anywhere in [32,38] and const at 74 anywhere in [L(cam),38].
frontier.next_probe: From the same def-order chassis, introduce a reg-reg copy consuming cam (and const) whose source is NOT dead at the copy — the precondition at local-alloc.c:1003-1007 — and read the resulting livelen off alloc.sh. Pure measurement: it either moves the two numbers into the window at 72 insns or it does not.

frontier.hypothesis: Route R3 (pre-RA scheduling moves a live length without moving a C statement) survives s6 untouched and now has twice the leverage.
frontier.mechanism: Live lengths are measured on the post-sched1 stream while emitted byte order is set by sched2, so two byte-identical C forms can present different pre-RA live lengths. Because the x2 is applied AFTER flow, a scheduling change that shortens the BASE by k shortens the doubled value by 2k. tools/sched_solver models both passes order- and clock-exactly and has still never been pointed at this function.
frontier.next_probe: Run tools/sched_solver on the def-order chassis and ask one question only: can any legal sched1 ordering move base(cam)/base(const) (or their doubled values) into [32,38] while leaving copy_end at 38 and the emitted stream byte-identical? Then confirm with inverse_compose.py classify that the residual is still RA-owned rather than PRE-RA.
